finding: The scrape-error theory is wrong: SpaceX really did acquire Anysphere/Cursor ($60B all-stock, agreed June 16, 2026 per SEC 8-K coverage, closed Aug 14, 2026 into a SpaceXAI unit). Separately, SpaceX also acquired xAI (announced Feb 2, 2026, ~$1.25T combined entity), so both SpaceX deals are real and the marker on Cursor is correct.

No acquisition of Apollo GraphQL found in two searches: 2026 PitchBook/Crunchbase profiles show it private and independent (~$1.5B valuation, $152M raised; YC/Insight/a16z investors); the only M&A on record is Apollo itself buying FathomDB and Percolate Studio. The acquired marker looks wrong as of Aug 2026.
Stripe acquired Metronome: announced December 2025 for a reported ~$1B, and Stripe's newsroom confirms the acquisition completed (early 2026).
Cloudflare announced the Replicate acquisition Nov 17, 2025 and closed it Dec 1, 2025; Cloudflare's FY2026 10-Q reports $57.4M total cash consideration.
Anthropic announced it is acquiring Stainless on May 18, 2026 (reported at >$300M via The Information); hosted Stainless products are being wound down.
OpenAI announced the Promptfoo acquisition March 9, 2026 (undisclosed terms; Promptfoo last valued $86M in July 2025); tech is being folded into OpenAI Frontier for agent security.
OpenAI announced March 19, 2026 that it will acquire Astral (uv, Ruff, ty); Charlie Marsh's team joins the Codex org, deal subject to regulatory approval at announcement.
Axon signed a definitive agreement to acquire Prepared (AI 911 communications) on Sept 23, 2025, expected to close early Q4 2025, and later reporting says the deal closed.
Databricks acquired Tecton, announced Aug 26, 2025 (structured as an acquisition of Tecton's assets per Fenwick, terms undisclosed), to power real-time data for AI agents.
Salesforce signed a definitive agreement Aug 18, 2025 to acquire Regrello for ~$900M cash and completed the acquisition Oct 1, 2025 (per Salesforce 10-Q and MarketScreener).
Miro announced it acquired Reforge on March 24, 2026 (team, learning platform, and AI product tools; Brian Balfour becomes Miro CGO). Note it is a partial deal: Reforge Learning stays independent.

Resourcely's own LinkedIn company page reads 'Resourcely (acquired by Anysphere)' and it announced the acquisition in July 2025; TechCrunch coverage framed it around Cursor hiring CEO Travis McPeak to lead security, but the company itself confirms an acquisition by Anysphere.
Meta acquired Limitless (fka Rewind, Dan Siroker), announced early December 2025; Pendant sales ended and the Rewind app was sunset with capture disabled Dec 19, 2025.

The a16z row is Exa Labs (exa.ai, AI search API) and it has NOT been acquired: it remains independent and recently raised a $250M round led by a16z at a $2.2B valuation. Likely confusion source: competitor Tavily was acquired by Nebius (~$275M, Feb 2026).
Grammarly announced its acquisition of Superhuman on July 1, 2025 (terms undisclosed; ~100-person team incl. CEO Rahul Vohra joined Grammarly).

a16z led Viggle AI's (Toronto, founder Hang Chu) $19M Series A in Aug 2024, and Viggle AI shows no acquisition (Tracxn profile lists it independent with 37 employees as of July 2026). The acquired Viggle is the unrelated older TV-rewards Viggle Inc., bought by Perk.com in 2016, so the acquired marker is a wrong-company artifact.
Yes: Sky is MakerDAO's rebrand (Sept 18, 2024; MKR converts to SKY at 1:24,000, DAI to USDS), and a16z crypto bought 6% of MKR supply for $15M in 2018, so a16z's Sky row is the MakerDAO/Sky position.

There is a newer a16z-backed Seismic, but it is not defense/industrial/energy: it is Seismic (seismic.systems), an encrypted L1 blockchain for fintech privacy founded by Lyron Co Ting Keh; a16z crypto led its $7M seed (announced March 2025) and a further $10M round (Nov 2025, $17M total). Definitely not Seismic Software (sales enablement).

The a16z-backed Mercury is Mercury Technologies (startup banking, Immad Akhund): Wikipedia lists a16z as a returning investor in its March 2025 Series C, and it is NOT acquired; it is independent at a $5.2B valuation (Series D, May 2026), received conditional OCC approval for a national bank charter (April 2026), and itself acquired payroll startup Central (April 2026). No acquired a16z-backed Mercury was found, so the acquired marker looks wrong.

a16z's Medley is the NYC group-coaching platform founded by mother-daughter duo Edith Cooper and Jordan Taylor; a16z (Connie Chan, Anne Lee Skates) led its $3.7M seed announced Oct 2021. It is not the Japanese telemedicine company Medley.

a16z's Mosaic is Mosaic Building Group, the homebuilding construction-tech company founded by Salman Ahmad and Sep Kamvar: a16z led its $14.25M Series A (2020; a16z announcement by Anish Acharya, Sept 2, 2020) and it later raised a $44M Series B (Nov 2021). Not the fertilizer company, not MosaicML.

a16z's Arena is LMArena/Chatbot Arena (Arena Intelligence Inc.): a16z co-led its $100M seed with UC Investments (May 2025, $600M valuation), it rebranded to Arena at arena.ai on Jan 28, 2026, and raised a $150M Series A at $1.7B (Jan 2026, Felicis + UC Investments). It is NOT Arena AI / Arena Technologies (NYC hardware-testing, Pratap Ranade), whose investors are Initialized, Fifth Down, Goldcrest, Founders Fund with no a16z.

Could not confirm a16z backing for either Ghost: the B2B surplus-inventory marketplace (Dee Murthy/Josh Kaplan; active, $40M Series C led by L Catterton Oct 2024) lists USV, Cathay Innovation, Equal Ventures, Eniac as investors; Ghost Autonomy (Founders Fund/Sutter Hill/Coatue/OpenAI) shut down April 3, 2024 after raising ~$220M. No a16z 'Investing in Ghost' announcement exists on a16z.com, so which Ghost sits on a16z's list remains unresolved.

No formal shutdown announcement found in three searches, but strong wind-down signals through 2024: an SF Chronicle piece notes 'many of All Day's locations are now closed' with the company unresponsive to comment requests, its SF Uber Eats listing closed June 2024, and Yelp marks SF (Diamond St) and Berkeley locations CLOSED; aggregator profiles claiming 15 active locations appear stale. Shutdown likely but date unverified.

None of the guessed Waves are a16z's: Wave accounting (H&R Block 2019), Wave VR concerts (Maveron/Griffin-led), and Wave mobile money (Sequoia/Founders Fund/Stripe) show no a16z ties. The a16z-backed Wave* that was acquired is WaveForms AI (Alexis Conneau's audio-AI startup; a16z led its $40M seed, announcement Dec 2024), acquired by Meta on Aug 8, 2025 for Superintelligence Labs, and the row almost certainly refers to it.

a16z's Alta is the Sydney/San Francisco VR games studio behind 'A Township Tale': a16z (Andrew Chen) co-led its $12.4M seed with Makers Fund, announced Jan 26, 2022 at a $62M valuation (~$30M raised total per Tracxn). Not Alta Motors (e-moto, shut 2018, no a16z tie found) and not Jenny Wang's AI-stylist Alta (Menlo-led). No acquisition or shutdown news found for the VR studio.

a16z's Yellow is the genAI 3D-character startup (yellow3d.com, YellowSculpt; founded 2023; exclusive Tafi/Daz Studio partnership) whose $5M seed a16z Games led, per a16z's own announcement. Two searches found NO acquisition of it (site still live), so the acquired marker is uncorroborated; note an unrelated South African energy startup Yellow raised a Series C in Aug 2026.

Confirmed a16z backing: Nitra (NYC healthcare fintech, Visa-powered cards/expense tools for medical practices) announced a $62M seed (equity + debt) in August 2022 with investors including a16z and NEA; it later raised $187M more announced March 2026 ($22M Series A Aug 2025, $50M Series B, plus debt/warehouse). Safe to restore the row.

Thingy Thing Inc. is NOT Stir: SEC EDGAR (CIK 0001760516, Los Angeles, DE-incorporated 2018) shows its officers are Maximillian Hellerstein and Cyrus Summerlin (Down to Shop, then Extra, the credit-building debit card, with co-founder Biren Shah), with a16z GP Anish Acharya as director; its July 16, 2021 Form D sold $14.55M, matching the ~$14.5M 2021 round, and the entity was renamed ALIGNED Co by its April 2022 Form D ($96.3M sold). Stir (Joseph Albanese) is a different company (Homebrew-led seed; a16z Series A at ~$100M valuation per The Information).

Yes: a16z's American Dynamism practice led Odyssey's $4.75M seed, announced October 2022 (not 2023); Odyssey is the New York-based school-choice/ESA platform founded by Joseph Connor (2021), later raising a $10M Series A in May 2024 (Tusk-led, with a16z's Katherine Boyle participating) and administering ESA programs including Texas's $1B TEFA.
